purpose: R1.1-B: direct evidence for the deletion-retry mechanism behind B9R2a/B9R2b, with honest limits.
errorNature: The EPERM in every drill comes from the darwin kernel denying unlink(2) on an APFS file carrying the user-immutable flag (chflags uchg). It is a real filesystem failure; only the flag timing is scenario-controlled. No error is simulated in JavaScript.

tracingAvailability.consequence: per-attempt syscall observation is impossible in this environment; mechanism-level claims rest on the rm() public contract with second-scale timing margins, and the product-path first-attempt ordering remains PARTIAL

EXP1_rmTransientRecovery.design: fs.promises.rm(dir, {recursive, force, maxRetries: 5, retryDelay: 1000}) on a dir whose deps/locked.js carries uchg from t=0; flag cleared at +3.5s. Linear backoff puts attempts at ~0/1/3/6/10/15s.
EXP1_rmTransientRecovery.proof: rm succeeded at ~6s, ~2.5s AFTER the clearance: attempts at 0/1/3s must have failed against the still-set flag, and at least one attempt happened after clearance. Both 'first attempts hit the protection' and 'deletion was re-attempted' hold at the rm() contract layer.

EXP2_rmExhaustionBoundedObservation.design: same rm() with the flag held; bounded at 45s.
EXP2_rmExhaustionBoundedObservation.finding: On darwin/Node v22.23.4, fs.promises.rm with maxRetries:5, retryDelay:1000 against a user-immutable file did NOT reject within 45s, although the retry loop demonstrably runs (EXP1 succeeds mid-window). The naive 'linear backoff exhausts at ~15s' reading of the docs did not reproduce at this delay. Recorded as observed platform behavior; NOT attributed to PR #38.

EXP3_productCloseDecomposition.design: product app.close() via createConsumerViteServer with optimizeDeps.include (no browser), identical setup except the uchg flag.

EXP4_unitRmWindow.design: unit fs.promises.rm(dir, {recursive, force, maxRetries: 5, retryDelay: 10}) on a uchg dir - the product's exact parameters.

b9r2bDurationAttribution.question: why did permanent-EPERM rounds take ~6.7-6.9s?
b9r2bDurationAttribution.answer: unit rm(5,10) with a uchg file rejects after 6.69-6.74s (EXP4); product close() flagged = 6.73-6.81s (EXP3, lab B9R2b 6.73-6.81s, public driver 6803ms); product close() unflagged = 3-4ms (EXP3 control). The entire delta is the rm() retry/backoff window; drain and Vite close contribute ~3ms in this path. The window is bounded (~6.8s << the 15s shutdown deadline) and ends in a visible EPERM rejection with cleanupIncomplete=false - no other wait or timeout path is involved.
b9r2bDurationAttribution.note: Node's documented 'linear backoff' would naively predict ~150ms at retryDelay:10; the empirically observed window is ~6.7s. That is a Node/darwin implementation behavior recorded as observed, not explained, and it is not a #38 defect: the product contract (reject, retain cache, visible failure) held in 3/3 lab rounds + the independent driver run.

claims.firstAttemptReturnsRealEperm: CONFIRMED (kernel EPERM from APFS user-immutable flag, not simulated)
claims.rmRetriesAfterFailure: CONFIRMED at rm() contract layer (EXP1 success ~2.5s after clearance)
claims.closeResolvesAndCacheFullyRemoved_produc: CONFIRMED (B9R2a lab 3/3 + public driver b9r2a: close resolved, cache fully removed)
